beats.name: George T. Doran
beats.role: consultant and former corporate planning director at Washington Water Power, writing in Spokane

beats.text: In the original, the A did not mean Achievable. It meant Assignable: who is actually going to do it.
beats.note: Doran's five were Specific, Measurable, Assignable, Realistic and Time-related. Achievable and Relevant came later.

beats.context: the length of the Management Review article that introduced SMART, pages 35 and 36 of the November 1981 issue.

beats.text: Doran wrote that the acronym does not mean every objective will have all five criteria.
beats.note: Many people still assume all five are compulsory.

beats.text: Researchers reviewing its use in physical activity programmes have pointed out it was never built on theory or experimental evidence.
beats.note: It began as advice for managers writing objectives, not as a tested method.

beats.line: SMART goals were never meant to tick every box.
